text: A pleasure, a pleasure! I am Guidan. Or one of four Guidan. We're two pairs you see, all brothers, all in the same business. If you find yourself in anywhere but the Slums or Hub, feel free to find us!

Alpharius-1, firstborn of the firstborn, though, I must admit, not the first born here in the city. Merely the firstborn. Confused? My apologies. Perhaps a simpler tongue? I am the first son of the High Foremer and the Archcanon, a pure fabricant, born of matrix-rending and nursed in molten steel. Dramatic, but true. These houses are as old as the clockmarrow that ticks through me.
Just a happily married fabricant, sera! And I hope to keep it that way, if you understand.
Uh, Venluen-21? That's who I am.
Ah, how rude of me. I forget myself. I am Kthardz Hrk-zet, at your service.
Abahman-7643, fisherman and sailor. I've been sailing this ocean for years with not an end in sight! But still I persist. What are we without hope, after all?
I am a statue, so I can't talk. Forget this conversation.
I am Ashzastzati, and not some pathetic body made of metal! I damn the wizard who thought himself clever enough to trap my soul, and use it to power this machine.
Alcolan-784, with his belly full 'o spirits and his spirits high on belly spirits or something. Yeah. I'm drunk on my own booze.
I am Nelos-11. And I am Nelos-12. We're a fabricant, singular. And trust me, neither he, nor I, like it very much.

Sunburned. You've heard of that? Happens to fair skinned people. Heard there's dunmer out there with skin black as night. All because of the sun.
Anyways. I get sunburned. I don't peel or hurt though. See, we're made of metal. Hot metal just gets hotter. Hot enough metal melts things. That's what I do. Melt things.
Transicant.

I am one of Seht's earlier Transicants, a relic of a time when he was known by that name still. It is a pity that you did not know him in the full flush of his divinity. His mind shone more brilliantly than Magnus itself, and he could fathom all the depths of the ocean.

My name is irrelevant, as are my origins. Merely know that I was a follower of Sotha Sil, perhaps one of his greatest students in fact. To him, I became a treasure, an ally, and upon my would-be-death, a test. I am the first fabricant, though, if we are to use the proper terminology, I am a transicant. I am the Archcanon, ruler of this city-in-a-city, and the final word on religious matters.

Salms-6, former shopkeeper's assistant, reduced to begging in the street. And here I thought this city was so understanding. Bah. I stand by what I say, only a fool likes gears, sprockets are for the wise and educated.
They used to call me Maggothe-37, though my name is now meaningless, like so much else. I've become a freak, I'm become far too attractive! My life, my dreams, all pointless.

Golamus-15, and my matrix number is... Well it isn't really important is it? My neighbors call me "The Mad Plant Wizard" though I suspect they're jealous; everyone is after a while! And there is so much to be jealous of.
I am %name, I serve Almalexia as one of Her Hands.

Yes! To metal! Wherever I go, metal flies at me, sticks to me, and won't leave me be! And in this city, there is metal everywhere! Entire houses bend to me as I walk down a street, my lover had to have her arms removed, just to escape me! I'm a freak, a walking disaster! Please, I beg you, if by death or by miracle, give me a way to be free of this horrible curse.
I have heard of your success in the Industrial District. You should not hold any ill will towards the Overclockers though. All fabricants desire to experiment, for their curiosity is their curse.
The broken repaired.
Devout but foolish in the generators. Dangerous. Unstable. Stop them. No time. Go. The way is open.

Home to the shops and foundries of our great city. Always busy, and like many busy things, it takes quite a bit of energy. So it is worrisome than the once ever-working Industrial District has now found itself the victim of power outages. Speak to the High Foremer, for they make their home there, and discover the source of these power fluctuations. If you were to stop them, the machines of that district would function properly. Speak to my counterpart in the Industrial District, the High Foremer, about it.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Industrial District
text: Now the two main attractions are the Offices of the High Foremer, which is that building in the center of the district, the one with the two smokestacks. The Foremer is almost always busy, but if you have official business or a breeding request, they'll listen. Finally, the two big buildings connected by the pipeline are the headquarters of the Overclockers, the local engineering-mystic faction. They offer enchanting and augmentation services to those who can afford it.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Industrial District
text: The first, of course, are your basic services. The local smith can be found behind the foundry sector, on the southeast side of the district, the apothecary is the large building in the northeast corner, and the clothier sits on the northwest corner, near the High Foremer's Offices. The big building with all the pipes is the local tavern, the Gear and Sprocket. Good drinks if you're thirsty. Cheap too.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Industrial District
text: This, friend, is the Industrial District. Fabricants are natural experimenters, and so this part of the city exists to give those who work in experiment groups space! Many foundries and bays are found here, where fabricants are employed or otherwise work. There are several points of interest for a visitor to the city; let me go over them.

The Industrial District is where the larger bays for group projects are kept; experiments or constructions too big for any one fabricant to complete on his own. It's filled with laboratories, workshops, and shops for all the things necessary to keep the district afloat. Alchemical reagents, equipment, and so forth. You'll also find offices of the High Foremer there.
We transicants are rare, as such an honor must be undertaken only by the Clockwork God himself. I was one of his greatest students, and now, I am one of his greatest assets.

There are more than just created mer-machines in this city, Nerevar. While the will of the Foremer and the unseen hands of the Regent are the mother and midwife of most of the populous, there are many other types of creations that live in this city. There are replicants, Intelligences, the Angry Bones, and myself, a transicant. I am a normal mer, born under normal circumstances, whose body and mind were taken into an incredible machine, and thus, am no longer mortal.

When useful, they are beautiful, when not, they are horrible. Replicants are mechanical copies of an individual, often of significance to Sotha Sil, such as a lover, an advisor, or a friend. They are built often to guide us, but once they serve their purpose, they are most often discarded, for a copy of something that is not that something can often become dangerous. I have heard you yourself have encountered several of these rogue replicants, down in the depths of the experiment.
Perhaps you do not recall, but recently I gave you instruction in the great foundry. You sought to cure the tree of life. And now, it seems again your arboreal skills are required.
The matter was dealt with.

We fabricants are people of invention and experimentation. Even machineless we invent and create new flora and fauna. Such a new strain has been developed, and perhaps it is the source of the infection. Find it, inspect it, destroy it if necessary. It lies on the western side of this district.
Already both you and he have assisted it in its goals. But now that you know the truth, you may cure the disease once and for all.

My poor Gardener thought to transfer the infection from me to himself, assured in his power that he could handle it. But it has failed. While the wound, the original source of the infection, is gone, the disease itself has merely found a new host, and one that is unaware of such a thing at that. An infection is alive, %PCRace, understand? It seeks, like all life, to grow and spread. Now believing himself to be fighting the infection, it has subtly spurred his mind towards increasing it.

You saw WHAT? That area is specifically closed off for a reason! How dare you-
Oh I suppose there's no point hiding things is there? Yes, we know about the power core. Our own local generator is created in its image, but understand we are not collectively to blame! It is that trio and their machinations!

I suppose, if it is for the good of the city, I can tell you. A trio of our once-finest engineers managed to discover a lost duct that lead to an enormous source of energy. 'Imagine such power in the hands of the people' they said. We only sought to replicate its design for our own experiments, I didn't realize they'd be willing to go back to the damn thing and start worshipping it!
What? No uh, I mean, I've heard of it, but we've nothing to do with such things. Now leave, you ask the wrong questions.

Though smaller versions exist, ultimate the city of Sotha Sil is fed by one massive power core. At least, it is rumored to be. No one has ever seen it. Perhaps the Overclockers might know more, perhaps not.
Power core? Like something to generate power, yes? That sounds like a big public project. Grand Gothaman would know more about something like that.

Correct. I hear you are a slayer of monsters, or otherwise fearsome beasts. Think of this like slaying a beast of society, with similar metaphors applying. And of course, like any other beast, you must track it, with our help.

Partially destroyed skeletal spirits. They reform into smaller, spider-like creatures. Because of their partial nature, they at times randomly fade out of existence, effectively going invisible. Very horrifying, and attracted to illusion magic.

Yes! I've got Foglern's Retroactive Spontaneous Dehydration sickness! It's characterized by excessive sniffing, shortness of breath, and glowing eyes, and I have all three of those! It's horrible. Last week I had Mumples, the week before that Slowwire, and now this!
We settled that, friend, nice and well we did too.
Dead, eh? Glad we reached an understanding, friend, here's your money.
You know what I mean, friend. Free the city from its chains by killing the head of the Abstemious, and the leader of the Overclockers.

It's simple, friend. This city's got the stink of two big factions, the Overclockers, and the Abstemious. Both of them constantly fight, keeping us honest working fabricants in the dirt, dying for their causes. What we need is a fresh start, and to do that, both leaders of both factions need to die, understand? Of course, if you do understand, you'll find yourself a little bit richer.
Again, I am quite grateful, as grateful as those thieves will be sorry!

Oh it feels good to feel my arms once more! It feels good to even have arms to feel with. Perhaps I was wrong to seek death, the feeling of living is enough after such an ideal! Thank you, friend, I know this isn't much, but it was one of the few unique things those fetchers didn't take! Speaking of which, I must go locate a blunt object, as revenge is in the air!

player-> RemoveItem "sotha_bodypart1" 1

text: Several troublemakers made off with and eventually, no doubt, sold my body. Look in various shops around the city, find it! When you have a full body, return to me, and perhaps I might be whole once more!

Here I was, thinking it all too much! So, I made a noose, and hung myself. But it seems that breath is not something I as a fabricant needed. So I hung here, alive and bored. Word seemed to reach some less-than-desirables, and they raided my house, and stole everything except my neck and head! Now I hang here, a shell of a man, seeking his lost body.
But you, yes, yes, you could help! Find my body parts and return them to me! Those fools no doubt sold them to merchants, so check there!
Hm. You know, right now I am experimenting with the effects of spells on a living body. Would you be interested in being my helper?

Every mer who walks this street seems funny, quirky, entertaining, yes? You laugh, but you laugh at a sickness in their souls. We are quirky because we are malfunctioning. We have reached the ends of our minds, every last one of us fabricants, yet still the experiment continues! But why, you wonder? The Clockwork God is not cruel, %PCName, only curious, and with curiosity comes absent-mindedness. The experiment continues because he has forgotten to shut us down. We exist, because he does not care anymore.

Of course! The King in Quartz is always experimenting, just as you and I are always breathing! Everything he does is for the sake of experimentation, be it his apotheosis, his world, or his people. Is he without love? Perhaps not, but we, like all else, are just creations to him. We have our use, and thus he uses us, we have love to give, and thus he loves us. But we were created for a purpose, and perhaps that purpose has reached its end. You find it hard to believe? Then look around you.
Please, meet me outside after 9 PM.

They say that the killer who killed those other poor girls has been taking their limbs before the Watchmen show up! I've got such great limbs, he's sure to come after me. Please, meet me outside the club tonight, after 9 PM! I want someone to escort me home...
(You feel your energy draining out of you, and you slump to the ground)
result_script:
Disable
FadeOut, 2
StartScript Sotha_Mazeteleport
FadeIn, 2
Goodbye

text: I shall take that as a yes! Don't blink!
That's fine, it's no plating off my machinery if you don't want to go.
I'm going to completely regret this...
Are you ready to go?
I'll blindfold you and take you there tonight, after 8 and before 12, if you really want to, but be warned some of the people there are... less than desirable.

Backwards fools. They're unwilling to think for themselves, and their holier-than-thou attitude is the worst of it. They say nothing worth listening to, so I wouldn't bother talking to them if I were you.

God is Perfection. How can it be otherwise? He created a perfect clockwork city in his perfect clockwork realm, and we fabricants are his issue. Thus created by the hand of God, how can we alter our forms? To do so would be a sign of grave disrespect to the Clockwork King of the Three-in-One. We therefore abstain from modifying our bodies while meditating upon his commandments. We watch, we wonder, we build, and, when necessary, we are unafraid to tear down.

The Abstemious are one of the two major factions in the city. They believe that the body is sacred, and thus should not be modified. Instead, they seek perfection through spiritual and natural enlightenment. Many healers and farmers support them, and they are heavy naturalists. Their headquarters is located in the Residential District. They are also bitter rivals with the Overclockers, and the two often clash.
That will do. Now relax, close your eyes, and I shall begin the process.

text: Very well.
Very well. Relax, close your eyes, and I shall begin the process.

text: If you receive this augmentation, your speed and agility will be increased by a small amount. It will cost you 100,000 gold. Do you wish to do this?
If you receive this augmentation, your speed and agility will be increased by a small amount. It will cost you 100,000 gold. Do you wish to do this?
I do not believe you can afford this augmentation. It is 100,000 gold.

The paths to his workshop are many, and many of those many lie unknown to me. However, I do know of one way, a portal in the Clocktower, which leads to the Underconstruction, which itself would lead you to the mainframe of the entire city. Though I will not grant you access to that portal as it is, at the moment, far too unstable.
Sotha Sil is our god and maker, the clockwork city is named after him, and we all respect and seek to emulate his work.
The Lord Sotha Sil is a great mage and a member of the Blessed Tribunal. He lives in his Clockwork City, and is rarely seen in Morrowind.
You are not clever.
That joke is tiresome.
This is the island of Solstheim, a jewel of an island and home to the Skaal. We settled here many generations ago.

If the tree dies as a seedling or fully grown tree, it will take a full stage to die. Killing it as a sapling will allow you to harvest it. You may replant a sapling or seed in cleared soil, on the second stage, provided the seedling has been killed. If you prune and kill the tree in its third stage, the fourth stage will have proceed a new life seed. Finally, if you wish, you may travel to the first stage and reset everything, provided you've pruned the seedling. As I promised, here is a pair of shears.

This area is named the Garden of Akatosh because one is able to travel through time, in four stages, each farther along in time then the other, at each containing the Flesh Tree at different stages of life. At all times, there must be a pure full grown tree at stage 3 for the manufactory to work. One can use a pair of shears, which I have provided, to prune away and kill the tree at the first, second, and third stages. However, the tree has an odd life cycle.

Well, we are friends, and there can be no secrets between friends, eh? I do not fully understand why the tesseroot was removed from the Aboretum, as the properties it contains are extremely powerful. While useless as an alchemical ingredient, ingesting a tesseroot seems to imbibe some piece of magical knowledge. I've learned so much simply from sprinkling bits of it into my dinner!

I'm afraid it's a secret project of mine, and we really don't know each other well enough to talk about such a thing. Suffice to say, if I can divulge its secrets, I can change the fate of the city itself.
I am glad that the Arboretum once again grows. Even in a world of machine, there should be some life.
The diseased, cured.
The diseased.

The source of life in the city of machines. It is here that trees and livestock were grown, to feed and supply the city. I am afraid this may no longer be the case. The Aboretum is dying, though nothing is reportedly broken, and oil still pumps to feed the exports of the city. If you were to stop whatever is choking the trees of that district, then its forests would flourish once again. The overseer of the Arboretum, the Gardener, would know more.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, The Arboretum
text:
Welcome, friend, to the district of growth and life, the Arboretum! There's not many buildings of interest here; it's a working-class district. However, the center tower is the main conservatory, and home to the overseer of this district, the Gardener.
What you should be wary of is that in order to house so much to feed a city so large, space is not correct in the Arboretum. Houses are bigger on the inside, and some connect to each other's entrances in nonsensical ways. Take care where you step.
The Arboretum feeds the city. The fleshy parts of it, at least. The main conservatory is where our food is grown and our livestock kept, and the oil-pumps direct the flow of oil throughout the city.
I wish you luck in the lower levels.

You do make a convincing argument. Perhaps there is something of infectious value deep within the depths. Very well, the four entrances to the lower levels are on the four corners of this island, on top of the farms. This key will let you in.

Access to the lower levels? Why? There is nothing down there, nor do I think the infection would come from there. I'm sorry, %PCName, but unless you can convince me otherwise, I see no reason to look there.
Seek out the oil flow, the fabricant farm, and the new strain of experimental trees, and see what might be seen.

Yes, the source! If the purpose and reason of this infection is located, and then removed, the Arboretum would heal. 
But we are lacking in knowledge of the source's location and nature. Luckily, I have my hints. Three possible locations, a blocked oil flow near the canals, a wrecked indoor fabricant farm, and a new strain of plant all might hold the key. I wish for you to investigate these possibilities.

And such an infection it is! You see, %PCName, while so much of this great realm is cold metal, the warmth of life beats through this district. And all this life is connected, one massive creature from whose arms we prune and grow that which feeds the city. But now it is sick. Not dying, but like anything sick, if it is not treated, it will die. You can go where I cannot, and therefore, you must assist in me in destroying the source of this infection.

Shock based magics power both the city and the guards. A high enough shock may overload and shut them down. If one could, say, redirect a power surge, it would disable the Watchmen standing guard, allowing you to slip past. 
Hm.
Yes, this might work. Find a lightning rod near the wrecked building you must enter. Attach this redirector, and wait for a surge. Then slip inside and find the Overclockers, and stop them before it is too late.

Yet another dead end. Whoever is behind this, or otherwise responsible, is quite good at covering their tracks, but perhaps not as good as they may think. You see, someone is spreading rumors, and to those who dig deep enough into the rumor mill will find the one who laid the seed, or otherwise started this whole mess.
Hm? Oh those things. Thought they were a novelty or a joke. I'm afraid I can't help you though, it was an anonymous commission, so I've no idea who asked for it. Sorry.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Industrial District, Suleri Printing
text: Talk to the headman about something like that, he's the one that manages orders.

Again we meet! After our last encounter I'd expect you to come to me, I seem to be up to my hair in conspiracy. Precisely why I began to ponder the situation. Are you a fan of logic, %PCRace? I am, and the fact that everything recently seems to point to me as the villain behind all this terrible strife in our district. Which is why, I must say, I am innocent. Think about it. Do you really think someone able to manipulate a social upheaval of this magnitude would so obviously leave his mark?

Words have power, and the ability to inspire, or otherwise spur to action. And though I have not read any myself, I hear that a few words have graced the residents of the Residential district, and many are, as some might say, 'fired up' over these words. Find the writer of them, and you will find, perhaps, the source of conflict.

Yes, that is what he said. We share a body, but not a mind. We lived with it at first, but after all this time, we've begun to get on each other's nerves. Nerve.
Hmmmm...
It is yours now. There are not many places to sleep in the city, and as such, it will no doubt be useful to you.

Fyr Manor is the residence of Lord Fyr, an old friend of our Lord Sotha Sil. He has not been here in over a century, though, so his house is essentially abandoned. It's probably one of the most advanced structures in the City proper, even despite its age.

Well, why not.
I'm not really familiar with daedric princesssss, but I underssssstand that one of them hasssssse followersssss that, every full moon, turn into an animal. I have never worssssshipped princessss, but I mysssself have sssssuch a condition, and ever full moon I turn into a hulking fabricant. It wouldn't be sssoooo bad, but farmerssssss always want to usssse me for ssssomething.
We're not really friendssssss, ssso no go. I do appreciate the company though.
Your help was most appreciated, wanted, or welcome.
Indeed, you have competed, finished, or succeeded. I have getting readings from all five measurers, as expected. Your reward, treasure, or fund, sera. A free coupon for an augmentation.
In high elevated points of each district, seek a container or barrel to put the daedron-aethernon measurers in. There is one in each district, other than the slums.

(She holds up a cube) You see this? It is a daedron-aethernon measurer, number-taker, or searcher. Placed in a high position, it can measure energy readings, something we overclockers sorely need. Placed in all districts besides the slums lie containers adapted, rebuilt specifically, to use these measurers. Reaching them is a problem however. We would like someone like you to take five of these, and place them in those containers, receptacles, or barrels. You will be rewarded of course.
PERHAPS. ANOTHER. DAY. THEN.

*There is the sound of someone exhaling*
VERY. WELL. IT. IS. DONE. YOU. MUST. LIVE. WITH. THE CONSEQUENCES.
WILL YOU SHUT DOWN THE WATCHMEN, AND LEAVE THE CITY TO THE DEVICES OF THE INSANE?

We of Sotha Sil are half-mer, half-machine, people who live in service to the Clockwork God. We are content in our city, and would rather experiment and research the arcane then muddle in the affairs of those from the other world.
All creations are eventually destroyed, whether it be by the hand of their creator or not. They prepare for that day constantly in the hope of surviving the aftermath.
All creations are eventually destroyed, whether it be by the hand of their creator or not. We prepare for that day constantly in the hope of surviving the aftermath.

cell_filter: Sotha Sil, Clockwork City, Temple District
text: Survivalists are what they are. They take "Tear Down" as less a commandment and more of a prophecy. We are, after all, Lord Sotha's creations, so they reason that he will eventually destroy us just as he has created us. They gather arms and test their strength, not that it would be of use against Lord Sotha, but to survive the aftereffects of his wrath.

Survivalists are what they are. They take "Tear Down" as less a commandment and more of a prophecy. We are, after all, Lord Sotha's creations, so they reason that he will eventually destroy us just as he has created us. They gather arms and test their strength, not that it would be of use against Lord Sotha, but to survive the aftereffects of his wrath.

We take the bones of the dead. We sell them. This angers the bones, they leave the catacombs, and our work may be done in peace.
Leave.
It's no concern of yours, %PCRace.
Both... of... us... are... experts... on... consciousness... and... metaphysics. We... collectively... assist... the... Archcanon... with... his... duties.
You know I don't need to do anything me! It's all a dream, so why work? I'll be waking up soon enough.
Stacking. Stacking. Everything stacking not crazy shut up don't talk can stack anything but NEED concentration can't concentrate when you stop stacking by talking stop talking.
We can do anything. We are three men with one soul. We are perfect in group projects. Just do not hit us please. We only ask for a room and food. And no torture or experimentation
I trade anything! You've got it, I'll buy it. I've got it, I'll sell it! Today only!
*Clank clank clank clank clank clank clunk*
I fall? Is that really a trade? Falling. Because it's all I do. It's anyone ever does. Fall. Fell. Foll? Foll isn't a word, nevermind.

I am afraid with my condition, contagious as it is, I cannot work. I must sit at my home and sleep. I do take walks sometimes, as everyone knows walks are good for you. It doesn't help though. My condition is probably incurable.
Greatest lover in the city, and there's no finer trade than that. Nor is there no finer lover, but I already mentioned that.

They called me insane for a while, Broken even. Oh but I know blood better than any of them! And quartz? Quartz is but the frozen blood of Akatosh! So they put me in charge of managing time's blood. It has turned out well for all of us. Though especially me. All this blood, really.

I don't really remember, boy. I think I wrote a book on rewounds. Nasty things, they took my son, did you know that?
But rather interesting. I remember how me and the old clergy used to take the bodies down into the catacombs. Got interested in those things back then. Decided to study them. Yep.
Practioner of nonsense logic, which is not that foul unlogic that the rabid fruit and the crazed dwemer practice, oh no!

Since the existence of the catacombs, I have made it my business, and by extension, the business of the city, to research the undead that inhabit it. Bone stokers and bone welders, rewounds, mechascarabs, bonespiders, I know them all. The whole "lich" act is a sort of side effect. No way to understand the undead if you're not one of them, eh?

Never had a job, friend! Never needed one! You need a job to get money, you need money to buy food! But with me and food, there's never been much love. If I sees it, I can eats it. Ebony, diamonds, ten pounds of raw steel, give it to me and it's in my mouth! Makes for an easy living, I say!

While in the future I will become a stripper, for reasons I'm still not sure of, currently I am an unfortune teller. Though I'm not working at the moment, the city is about to go through a few changes after all.

I farm and raise verminous and hulking fabricants. Since I've always been good with the stock, my fabricants tend to be better quality than most, and I've made a comfortable living off doing so. The stock have always appreciated my abilities.
I drift. My condition makessssss it hard to find work. Or rather, I could find work, but it isssssn't the work I ssssshould be doing.

What else would a Guidan brother do but guide? Free information for newcomers and outlanders! We know all about the districts of each city, so if you seek out me or one of my siblings, we will be sure to give you integral information.
I cook, sweep, and make sure my husband keeps his nose out of... trouble, if you understand.
I... was working on automated cart systems. Now, not so much.

Mechanic, by trade, though these days I'm more of an amateur historian. And, I suppose, the de facto Dwemer diplomat to Sotha Sil, given that I'm the only one living here. Why, I can't imagine. One of the nicest Chimeri cities in Resdayn.
I fish, I used to do it to bring in the coin, but now I fish to eat! Luckily I always find crates floating around, full of food and drink.
I have to continually remind people that I am a statue in a park! Yet they seem to keep forgetting that statues don't talk!
I am a rapist. Of your corpse. Understand?
They call me the town drunk, but, but you know what? To be a drunk, I have to be sober sometimes! And hah, piss on them I ain't ever sober! Kinda wonder what it's like really.

Neither of us can really agree on a job. But two people in one body makes it look like we've got twice the memory. One of us talks, the other observes.
It's gotten us quite far in life.
Hot metal melts things. Like walls. On houses. Or vaults. Not much of a thief though. After all, I can just walk right in and take what I please.
Little of this. Little of that. Not much work for a superheating fabricant.
Foremer.

I am the Chief Foremer. I guide the souls of new Fabricants to their temporary vessels, aiding those who wish to create new life. It is complex and incredibly difficult, even after all these millenia, and I merely ape Sotha Sil's instructions but imperfectly. There are no easy births in the Clockwork City.
I am the Archcanon of Sotha Sil.

I used to be a shopkeeper's assistant. Then one day my employer and I decided to make small-talk. The topic turned to mechanisms, and eventually gears. I merely say that I prefer sprockets, and within a day, I've lost my job, people look at me with disgust, and I'm out begging for scraps. Let me tell you something, friend, keep your opinions hidden in this city, you'll be better off for it.

I'm an abomination, my attraction prevents me from living a normal life! Oh, to not have been spawned in a city of steel!
I mean, everything is made out of steel, yes?

I suppose you can consider me an alchemist, though in truth that's my profession. My profession defies conventional words, and thus, it can only be described! I am a Floral Engineer, and perhaps a saviour of these poor plants, rejected from the Aboretum for simply being different. But I understand them, I take them in, and I grow them, give them purpose and life. Unfortunately, many do not survive; however the holobulbs, the conductor shrubs, and the tesseroot all seem to be flourishing.
I'm a lover and a killer. What more is there in life?

Have you often heard that a realm and a God are one and the same? It is a similar concept for this city. The people here are the life of this city, like blood in a body. The people of this city are troubled, and thus, the city is sick, and many things do not function correctly. If you wished to use this portal without risk, you would have to ease the troubles of the city.

Once, Sotha Sil was like we are, the Lord Vivec and I. He spent time among these mortals, instructing them, counseling them, protecting them from harm. He may have loved them more than any of us, though I know not why. It has been many years since any have seen the Sorcerer, though. Many more since he took initiates into his service. I believe he grew weary of mortal imperfections, and retired to his Clockwork City, where he reshapes life, and some say the very world, into an image he finds pleasing.

Beautiful aren't they? Though, to the Aboretum, they were conventionally useless, and thus left to die in some forgotten bin. The light they absorb is projected back out, in the form of an image. Though I believe them to be broken, as they only ever project the green spheres, you see. Perhaps it is a sign; I must research that more.
We have discussed that matter.
Like a vein that blocks blood, a pump has stopped pumping the oil from which life flows! It is located in a house down in the canals of crude that surround this building. Find it and unblock it.
